items.question: What drove operating margin change as of FY2022 for 3M? If operating margin is not a useful metric for a company like this, then please state that and explain why.
items.gold:
Operating Margin for 3M in FY2022 has decreased by 1.7% primarily due to: 
-Decrease in gross Margin
-mostly one-off charges including Combat Arms Earplugs litigation, impairment related to exiting PFAS manufacturing, costs related to exiting Russia and divestiture-related restructuring
charges

agent.answer: Operating margin decreased from 20.8% in FY2021 to 19.1% in FY2022. The decline was driven by increased cost of sales (3.0% YoY increase due to PFAS litigation costs and raw material price hikes), higher SG&A expenses (6.1% YoY increase), and manufacturing headwinds from supply chain disruptions. A $2,724 million gain on business divestitures also reduced operating income in FY2022.
agent.calculation: Operating margin FY2021 = 7,369 / 35,355 * 100 = 20.84%, rounded to 20.8%; Operating margin FY2022 = 6,539 / 34,229 * 100 = 19.10%, rounded to 19.1%

- U.S. consumers and businesses serve as the primary domestic market through USCS and CS segments

- Capital Expenditures: $23,087 million (from Cash Flows)
- Operating Revenues: $136,835 million 
- Total Assets: $379,680 million

CapEx-to-Revenue ratio = 23,087 / 136,835 * 100 = 16.9%
CapEx-to-Total Assets ratio = 23,087 / 379,680 * 100 = 6.1%

These ratios indicate Verizon invests approximately 16.9% of annual revenue and 6.1% of total assets into capital expenditures, characteristic of a capital-intensive telecommunications business.
